posts.cooked: So the Prime Warden Cosmic infinite loop instant win is still considered fair and legal after talking it over? I'm really having a difficult time understanding the rational behind allowing this to continue even after aproval from Christopher. posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Foote:

For reference, every single other instance of an infinite loop that has ever been found since the games initial creation has been overruled or changed to make it impossible to do. What exactly is the rational behind allowing this one and not any of the others ever found?

Not every other instance.  For instance, Absolute Zero with Twist the Ether or Imbued Fire can still do infinite damage when Fixed Point is in play, as near as I can tell.  But every other instance that can be initiated without a specific, nonpermanent villain or environment card in play has been clarified to not work.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
MindWanderer:
Foote wrote:
For reference, every single other instance of an infinite loop that has ever been found since the games initial creation has been overruled or changed to make it impossible to do. What exactly is the rational behind allowing this one and not any of the others ever found?  
Not every other instance.  For instance, Absolute Zero with Twist the Ether or Imbued Fire can still do infinite damage when Fixed Point is in play, as near as I can tell.  But every other instance that can be initiated without a specific, nonpermanent villain or environment card in play has been clarified to not work.

Fix Point's entire purpose for existing is to create crazy situations that would otherwise not be possible by the normal rules of the game. I think it would be fair to consider any Fix Point shenanigans exceptions to any conventional norm. Thats my take on it.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
Foote:

 

MindWanderer wrote:
Foote wrote:
For reference, every single other instance of an infinite loop that has ever been found since the games initial creation has been overruled or changed to make it impossible to do. What exactly is the rational behind allowing this one and not any of the others ever found?   
Not every other instance.  For instance, Absolute Zero with Twist the Ether or Imbued Fire can still do infinite damage when Fixed Point is in play, as near as I can tell.  But every other instance that can be initiated without a specific, nonpermanent villain or environment card in play has been clarified to not work.
Fix Point's entire purpose for existing is to create crazy situations that would otherwise not be possible by the normal rules of the game. I think it would be fair to consider any Fix Point shenanigans exceptions to any conventional norm. Thats my take on it.

Also, eliminating the Isothermic Transducer/Fixed Point loop would require major errata on at least one of the cards involved.  There is no amount of rules bending that can fix that loop.
